children.text: A circular binary contains point masses M1 and M2 separated by a. Its centre of mass is the origin of co-rotating xy coordinates, with M1 on negative x and M2 on positive x. The effective potential per test mass includes gravity and centrifugal potential. Mass transfer from M2 to M1 has small rate β>0, so orbits remain nearly circular. Assume conservative transfer and conserved total orbital angular momentum in A4. In A5 use a steady thin blackbody accretion disc close to M1, ignore M2's pull and gas heat capacity, and balance the local loss of circular orbital energy with radiation from both faces. For PSR J2215+5135 use MNS=2.27M☉, MS=0.33M☉, P=4.14 h, M☉=\(1.98\times10^{30}\) kg, β=\(9\times10^{-10}\) M☉/yr, G=\(6.67\times10^{-11}\) SI and σ=\(5.67\times10^{-8}\) SI. In B, a spherical isolated star obeys p=Kργ. Central values are pc and ρc, and outward acceleration is positive.
Only here let M2=M1/3. Find x0/a to two significant figures for gas overflow from M2 towards M1.
Find da/dt and dP/dt under slow conservative mass transfer.
Find temperature at disc radius r.
Calculate T at r=a/10 for the specified binary.
An explosion leaves mass M1′ and relative speed v′ at separation a. Find the limiting v′ for a bound binary and the limiting M1′ if the explosion is isotropic.
Find g(r) close to the centre.
Construct r0=Gℓpcmρcn with length dimensions and no numerical prefactor.
Put x=r/r0 and u=ρ/ρc. Find A1 and A2 in d[A1 du/dx]/dx+A2u=0.
For γ=2 write u=f(x)/x and find f using a regular centre with u(0)=1.

children.text: Use the initial slope of the supplied du/dx plot to determine γ to three significant figures.
Near the centre let r̃=r[1+ε(t)] with |ε|≪1. Find ρ̃ and g̃ to first order.
Find d²r̃/dt² in terms of g̃,ρ̃,K,γ and the density gradient at fixed time.
Derive the equation for ε, the limiting γ and the oscillation angular frequency.

statement.text:
Black widow pulsar
A circular binary contains point masses M1 and M2 separated by a. Its centre of mass is the origin of co-rotating xy coordinates, with M1 on negative x and M2 on positive x. The effective potential per test mass includes gravity and centrifugal potential. Mass transfer from M2 to M1 has small rate β>0, so orbits remain nearly circular. Assume conservative transfer and conserved total orbital angular momentum in A4. In A5 use a steady thin blackbody accretion disc close to M1, ignore M2's pull and gas heat capacity, and balance the local loss of circular orbital energy with radiation from both faces. For PSR J2215+5135 use MNS=2.27M☉, MS=0.33M☉, P=4.14 h, M☉=\(1.98\times10^{30}\) kg, β=\(9\times10^{-10}\) M☉/yr, G=\(6.67\times10^{-11}\) SI and σ=\(5.67\times10^{-8}\) SI. In B, a spherical isolated star obeys p=Kργ. Central values are pc and ρc, and outward acceleration is positive.
a-1. Rotating potential
Find φ(x,y) using M1,M2,G,a.
a-2. Axial potential sketch
For M1>M2 sketch φ(x,0).
a-3. Overflow point
Only here let M2=M1/3. Find x0/a to two significant figures for gas overflow from M2 towards M1.
a-4. Secular binary evolution
Find da/dt and dP/dt under slow conservative mass transfer.
a-5. Disc temperature law
Find temperature at disc radius r.
a-6. Observed-system estimate
Calculate T at r=a/10 for the specified binary.
a-7. Sudden mass loss
An explosion leaves mass M1′ and relative speed v′ at separation a. Find the limiting v′ for a bound binary and the limiting M1′ if the explosion is isotropic.
b-1. Central gravitational acceleration
Find g(r) close to the centre.
b-2. Density equilibrium equation
Write \(d[h_1(\rho,r)d\rho/dr]/dr+h_2(r)\rho=0\), identifying h1 and h2.
b-3. Central length scale
Construct r0=Gℓpcmρcn with length dimensions and no numerical prefactor.
b-4. Dimensionless equation
Put x=r/r0 and u=ρ/ρc. Find A1 and A2 in d[A1 du/dx]/dx+A2u=0.
b-5. Analytic density for γ=2
For γ=2 write u=f(x)/x and find f using a regular centre with u(0)=1.
b-6. Infer equation-of-state exponent

Use the initial slope of the supplied du/dx plot to determine γ to three significant figures.
b-7. Small homologous perturbation
Near the centre let r̃=r[1+ε(t)] with |ε|≪1. Find ρ̃ and g̃ to first order.
b-8. Perturbed shell acceleration
Find d²r̃/dt² in terms of g̃,ρ̃,K,γ and the density gradient at fixed time.
b-9. Radial stability criterion
Derive the equation for ε, the limiting γ and the oscillation angular frequency.

children.text: Set M=M1+M2, a1=M2a/M and a2=M1a/M, with Ω²=GM/a³. Then \[\varphi=-\frac{GM_1}{\sqrt{(x+a_1)^2+y^2}}-\frac{GM_2}{\sqrt{(x-a_2)^2+y^2}}-\frac{GM}{2a^3}(x^2+y^2).\] The centrifugal potential has a negative sign.

Draw downward divergences on both sides of x=−a1 and x=a2, and φ→−∞ as x→±∞ because of centrifugal potential. There is one local maximum in each of the three intervals separated by the two masses, at the three collinear Lagrange points. The central maximum is closer to the smaller mass.
The masses lie at −a/4 and 3a/4. With ξ=x/a, solve \(\frac{3}{4(\xi+1/4)^2}-\frac{1}{4(3/4-\xi)^2}-\xi=0\) between them. The inner stationary point is ξ≈0.3607, hence 0.36.

Conserved angular momentum is \(J=M_1M_2\sqrt{Ga/(M_1+M_2)}\). Using Ṁ1=β=−Ṁ2 gives \[\dot a=-2\beta a(1/M_1-1/M_2),\qquad\dot P=-3\beta P(1/M_1-1/M_2),\] where \(P=2\pi\sqrt{a^3/[G(M_1+M_2)]}\). For M1>M2 the separation and period grow.

The circular specific orbital energy is −GM1/(2r). An annulus releases GM1βdr/(2r²). Its two radiating faces have area 4πrdr. Thus \[T(r)=\left(\frac{GM_1\beta}{8\pi\sigma r^3}\right)^{1/4}.\] This uses the local energy model requested here, without the angular-momentum-transport correction of a detailed viscous-disc theory.
Kepler gives \(a=[GP^2(M_{NS}+M_S)/(4\pi^2)]^{1/3}\). Convert β to kg/s and P to seconds, giving \(T=[500\pi M_{NS}\beta/(\sigma P^2(M_{NS}+M_S))]^{1/4}\simeq9.0\times10^3\,\mathrm K\).

The new orbital energy is negative only for \(v^{\prime}<\sqrt{2G(M_1^{\prime}+M_2)/a}\). Isotropic rapid ejection produces no kick, so v′²=G(M1+M2)/a. The condition is \(M_1^{\prime}>(M_1-M_2)/2\). Equality in either condition is a parabolic, marginally unbound orbit.
Enclosed mass is approximately 4πρcr³/3, hence \(g=-4\pi G\rho_cr/3\).

Combine dp/dr=−GM(r)ρ/r² with M′=4πr²ρ and p=Kργ. Eliminate M to obtain \[\frac d{dr}\left(r^2\rho^{\gamma-2}\frac{d\rho}{dr}\right)+\frac{4\pi Gr^2}{K\gamma}\rho=0.\] Thus h1=r²ργ−2 and h2=4πGr²/(Kγ).
Matching mass, length and time exponents gives ℓ=−1/2, m=1/2, n=−1. Thus \(r_0=\sqrt{p_c/G}/\rho_c\).
Using pc=Kρcγ and the B3 scale, \[\frac d{dx}\left(x^2u^{\gamma-2}\frac{du}{dx}\right)+\frac{4\pi x^2}{\gamma}u=0.\] Thus A1=x²uγ−2 and A2=4πx²/γ.
The equation reduces to f″+2πf=0. Regularity gives f(0)=0 and u(0)=f′(0)=1. Hence \(f=\sin(\sqrt{2\pi}x)/\sqrt{2\pi}\).

Regularity imposes u′(0)=0. Expanding the dimensionless equation near zero gives \(3u^{\prime\prime}(0)+4\pi/\gamma=0\). The plotted initial slope of u′ is approximately −2.51, giving γ≈1.67. The official graphical acceptance interval is 1.64 to 1.70.
Mass conservation for a homologously expanded shell gives \(\tilde\rho=\rho(1+\epsilon)^{-3}\simeq\rho(1-3\epsilon)\). Fixed enclosed mass gives \(\tilde g=g(1+\epsilon)^{-2}\simeq g(1-2\epsilon)\).

Gravity plus pressure force per mass gives \[\ddot{\tilde r}=\tilde g-\frac1{\tilde\rho}\frac{\partial\tilde p}{\partial\tilde r}=\tilde g-K\gamma\tilde\rho^{\gamma-2}\frac{\partial\tilde\rho}{\partial\tilde r}.\]

The pressure acceleration scales as (1+ε)²−3γ, while gravity scales as (1+ε)⁻². Cancel equilibrium forces to find \[\ddot\epsilon=\frac gr(3\gamma-4)\epsilon=-\frac{4\pi G\rho_c}{3}(3\gamma-4)\epsilon.\] Stable restoring motion requires γ>4/3, and \(\omega=\sqrt{4\pi G\rho_c(3\gamma-4)/3}\). At γ=4/3 this linear model is marginal.

solution.text:
Black widow pulsar
a-1. Rotating potential
Set M=M1+M2, a1=M2a/M and a2=M1a/M, with Ω²=GM/a³. Then \[\varphi=-\frac{GM_1}{\sqrt{(x+a_1)^2+y^2}}-\frac{GM_2}{\sqrt{(x-a_2)^2+y^2}}-\frac{GM}{2a^3}(x^2+y^2).\] The centrifugal potential has a negative sign.
a-2. Axial potential sketch
Draw downward divergences on both sides of x=−a1 and x=a2, and φ→−∞ as x→±∞ because of centrifugal potential. There is one local maximum in each of the three intervals separated by the two masses, at the three collinear Lagrange points. The central maximum is closer to the smaller mass.
a-3. Overflow point
The masses lie at −a/4 and 3a/4. With ξ=x/a, solve \(\frac{3}{4(\xi+1/4)^2}-\frac{1}{4(3/4-\xi)^2}-\xi=0\) between them. The inner stationary point is ξ≈0.3607, hence 0.36.
a-4. Secular binary evolution

a-5. Disc temperature law
The circular specific orbital energy is −GM1/(2r). An annulus releases GM1βdr/(2r²). Its two radiating faces have area 4πrdr. Thus \[T(r)=\left(\frac{GM_1\beta}{8\pi\sigma r^3}\right)^{1/4}.\] This uses the local energy model requested here, without the angular-momentum-transport correction of a detailed viscous-disc theory.
a-6. Observed-system estimate
Kepler gives \(a=[GP^2(M_{NS}+M_S)/(4\pi^2)]^{1/3}\). Convert β to kg/s and P to seconds, giving \(T=[500\pi M_{NS}\beta/(\sigma P^2(M_{NS}+M_S))]^{1/4}\simeq9.0\times10^3\,\mathrm K\).
a-7. Sudden mass loss
The new orbital energy is negative only for \(v^{\prime}<\sqrt{2G(M_1^{\prime}+M_2)/a}\). Isotropic rapid ejection produces no kick, so v′²=G(M1+M2)/a. The condition is \(M_1^{\prime}>(M_1-M_2)/2\). Equality in either condition is a parabolic, marginally unbound orbit.
b-1. Central gravitational acceleration
Enclosed mass is approximately 4πρcr³/3, hence \(g=-4\pi G\rho_cr/3\).
b-2. Density equilibrium equation
Combine dp/dr=−GM(r)ρ/r² with M′=4πr²ρ and p=Kργ. Eliminate M to obtain \[\frac d{dr}\left(r^2\rho^{\gamma-2}\frac{d\rho}{dr}\right)+\frac{4\pi Gr^2}{K\gamma}\rho=0.\] Thus h1=r²ργ−2 and h2=4πGr²/(Kγ).
b-3. Central length scale
Matching mass, length and time exponents gives ℓ=−1/2, m=1/2, n=−1. Thus \(r_0=\sqrt{p_c/G}/\rho_c\).
b-4. Dimensionless equation
Using pc=Kρcγ and the B3 scale, \[\frac d{dx}\left(x^2u^{\gamma-2}\frac{du}{dx}\right)+\frac{4\pi x^2}{\gamma}u=0.\] Thus A1=x²uγ−2 and A2=4πx²/γ.
b-5. Analytic density for γ=2
The equation reduces to f″+2πf=0. Regularity gives f(0)=0 and u(0)=f′(0)=1. Hence \(f=\sin(\sqrt{2\pi}x)/\sqrt{2\pi}\).
b-6. Infer equation-of-state exponent
Regularity imposes u′(0)=0. Expanding the dimensionless equation near zero gives \(3u^{\prime\prime}(0)+4\pi/\gamma=0\). The plotted initial slope of u′ is approximately −2.51, giving γ≈1.67. The official graphical acceptance interval is 1.64 to 1.70.
b-7. Small homologous perturbation
Mass conservation for a homologously expanded shell gives \(\tilde\rho=\rho(1+\epsilon)^{-3}\simeq\rho(1-3\epsilon)\). Fixed enclosed mass gives \(\tilde g=g(1+\epsilon)^{-2}\simeq g(1-2\epsilon)\).
b-8. Perturbed shell acceleration
Gravity plus pressure force per mass gives \[\ddot{\tilde r}=\tilde g-\frac1{\tilde\rho}\frac{\partial\tilde p}{\partial\tilde r}=\tilde g-K\gamma\tilde\rho^{\gamma-2}\frac{\partial\tilde\rho}{\partial\tilde r}.\]
